route: Tier 5 (Temporary Worker - Creative and Sporting) visa, on a certificate of sponsorship; British and Irish citizens need only the Department for Enterprise's work permit

permit.applies: The performer applies for entry clearance on the UK Visas and Immigration website; a licensed Tier 5 sponsor first issues the certificate of sponsorship; the employer applies and pays for the work permit
permit.first: An offer of work and a certificate of sponsorship from a licensed sponsor

fees.what: Work permit grant or renewal (paid by the employer; British, Irish and other non-Isle of Man workers)

permit.eligibility: "You've been offered work in the UK as a sports person or creative worker"

sources.title: Isle of Man Government, Tier 5 – Temporary Workers
sources.said: A creative worker is someone who works in the creative industry, for example an actor, dancer, musician or film crew member. You must apply for a Tier 5 (Temporary Worker - Creative and sporting) visa if: You’ve been offered work in the UK as a sports person or creative worker … You need to have a certificate of sponsorship from a licensed sponsor before you can apply to come to the Isle of Man to work. … You can stay in the Isle of Man for up to 12 or 24 months (depending on the scheme you’re applying for) or the time given on your certificate of sponsorship plus 28 days, whichever is shorter. … You make an application for entry clearance to the Isle of Man at UK Visas and Immigration .

sources.title: Isle of Man Government, Visa application forms and fees
sources.said: CoS (Tier 5) Application for a Certificate of Sponsorship for a Tier 5 Worker £55

sources.title: Isle of Man Government, Work Permit fees (last updated 31 October 2017)
sources.said: An application for the grant or renewal of a work permit must be accompanied by a fee of £60. (The fee is the same irrespective of the duration of the permit). The fee is not refundable if the application is refused. The fee for a work permit is paid by the employer

sources.title: Isle of Man Government, Temporary Exemptions (last updated 28 February 2017)
sources.said: The following exemptions are for temporary employment for up to 48 days a year: … Theatrical and musical productions

note: Two permissions: immigration leave (Tier 5 creative, for passports other than British and Irish) and the Island's work permit (everyone who isn't an Isle of Man worker). The work permit's £60 fee is paid by the employer, and theatrical and musical productions are exempt from it for up to 48 days a year; the Tier 5 visa has no such exemption on the pages read.
